text:
devops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: KV cache continuous-batching spike detected in us-west-2. metric=kv_entries_total +720% over baseline, blockmgr_eviction_rate > 5x, 2s p99 token latency climbing. Auto-mitigation triggered

sara: I'm on it, checking service map. tagging @james for config hotfix + @li for runbook updates

james: pulling logs from model-prefetcher, I see a recent config flip that increased `prefetch_window_ms` from 50 -> 350 (rolled 03:12 UTC). lots of tiny keys created. suspect churn causing cache blowup

li: good find. I'll prepare a quick config cap. planning to throttle batch size and re-enable prefix coalescing for prefetcher

mike: can we do a non-disruptive rollout? prefer in-place config update w/o pod restarts if possible

james: doing `redwoodctl` patch now to cap batch.concurrency and max_batch_size for that deployment
```bash
# apply soft cap for model-prefetcher
redwoodctl set config --selector=service=model-prefetcher \
  --patch '{"batch": {"max_concurrency": 8, "max_batch_tokens": 1024}}'
```

li: also applying an eviction tweak on blockmgr: set `eviction.strategy=aggressive`, `block.target_bytes=131072` to trim small-key noise. hotpatching config map
```json
{"blockmgr": {"eviction": "aggressive", "block_target_bytes": 131072}}
```

sara: applied both patches. no pod restarts observed. watching metrics

james: metrics: kv_entries_total growth curve flattened within ~90s of patch. eviction_rate spiked briefly then normalized. token p50/p95 improved, p99 still high but trending down

devops-bot: Incident INC-1342 created and linked. Severity P2 assigned. Incident channel: #incidents-kv

tanya: CS: two customers reported 5xxs between 03:14-03:18 UTC (~3-4 minutes). I sent an initial heads-up note, will do a follow-up once we have RCA

customer-success-bot: Customer notification sent to affected tenants: "We're investigating increased errors and latency; temporary mitigation in progress. Will update within 30m."

li: quick root-cause hypothesis: metadata leak in block manager where `subscription_object` entries weren't being compacted for tiny prefetch keys, causing metadata to persist across blocks and inflate block index. PR to truncate stale metadata every 10k keys queued: PR #489

mike: PR #489 merged to staging. canary rollout to 5% traffic now. command: `deploy canary blockmgr --pct=5 --config=pr-489`

james: canary looks clean after 12m: blockmgr metadata size down 60% in canary pods. rolling to 25%

sara: good. ops checklist for handoff: 1) hotpatches applied (batch cap + aggressive eviction) 2) canary PR merged and rolling 3) monitor p99 and eviction_rate for next 2h 4) CS notified. I'm taking overnight ownership until morning oncall handoff

li: I'm adding runbook notes and the compact/trim steps to the runbook: <https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-metadata-trim>. also added commands to force-trim in emergency:
```bash
# emergency metadata trim
redwoodctl ops blockmgr trim-metadata --shard all --limit 10000
```

oncall-rotation-bot: Handoff scheduled: @mike will take pager at 08:00 UTC (duration 12h).

mike: I'll take the handoff and watch the canary/rollout for 2h post-handoff. if p99 doesn't fall below baseline+20% by 04:30 UTC, we'll revert prefetcher change and open a rollback PR

sara: noted. follow-up items: James to add sampling to prefetcher to avoid tiny-key storms; Li to harden blockmgr metadata lifecycle; CS will prepare post-incident customer note. Closing thread for immediate triage, moving to #incidents-kv for RCA docs

devops-bot: Incident updated: mitigations applied -> monitoring. Status: stabilizing.
